name: ripgrep
description: Recursively searches directories for a regex pattern and prints the matches, respecting your .gitignore by default.
why: It is the search tool we reach for first. Fast enough that you stop batching greps and just ask.
audience: Anyone who still greps large trees by hand and wants an instant search that respects .gitignore.

name: fzf
description: A general-purpose command-line fuzzy finder that plugs into shells, editors, and any pipeline that emits lines.
why: One binary that quietly upgrades history search, file jumping, and git checkout. Learn it once, use it everywhere.
audience: Terminal users who want fuzzy history search, file-jumping, and git checkout without memorizing exact paths.

name: htmx
description: Gives you AJAX, WebSockets, and server-sent events straight from HTML attributes, no build step required.
why: A reminder that a lot of interactive UI never needed a framework. Great for small, sturdy interfaces.
audience: Teams building small, sturdy UIs who don't want a full SPA framework's build step and bundle size.

name: Zod
description: TypeScript-first schema validation that infers your static types from a single source of truth.
why: Write the schema once and get parsing, validation, and types for free. It removes a whole class of drift.
audience: TypeScript teams tired of writing runtime validation and static types twice for the same shape.

name: Astro
description: A content-focused web framework that ships zero JavaScript by default and lets you bring any UI library you like.
why: It is what this very page is built on. The islands model makes fast, mostly-static sites the easy path.
audience: Teams building mostly-static, content-heavy sites who want islands of interactivity, not a full SPA runtime.

name: Playwright
description: Reliable end-to-end browser testing across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit through one consistent API.
why: Auto-waiting and honest tracing mean fewer flaky tests and faster answers when something breaks.
audience: QA and dev teams who want one API for end-to-end tests across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

name: DuckDB
description: An in-process analytical SQL database — think SQLite, but built for fast queries over local files.
why: Query a pile of CSV or Parquet files with real SQL and no server to stand up. It changes how you explore data.
audience: Anyone with a pile of CSV or Parquet files who wants real SQL without spinning up a database server.

name: Meilisearch
description: A fast, typo-tolerant search engine you can drop into an app and have returning relevant results in minutes.
why: Sensible defaults out of the box. You get search that feels good without tuning a heavyweight cluster.
audience: Teams adding search to an app who want typo-tolerant, relevant results without tuning a heavyweight cluster.

name: Caddy
description: A web server with automatic HTTPS. Sensible defaults get a real site online from a one-line config.
why: TLS certificates renew themselves and stay out of your way. The shortest honest path from box to live site.
audience: Anyone self-hosting a site who wants HTTPS to just work without touching Certbot or nginx configs.

name: Uptime Kuma
description: A self-hosted monitoring tool: a clean, friendly status page and alerting for the services you run.
why: Set it up in an afternoon and finally know when something is down before your users tell you.
audience: Self-hosters who want to know a service is down before a user tells them, without paying for a SaaS monitor.

name: Excalidraw
description: A virtual whiteboard for hand-drawn-style diagrams — fast, collaborative, and usable offline.
why: The lo-fi look keeps diagrams feeling like thinking, not deliverables. Perfect for sketching a system live.
audience: Teams who want to sketch a system or flow live on a call without their diagram looking like a deliverable.

name: Biome
description: One fast toolchain that formats and lints JavaScript and TypeScript, replacing several tools with a single binary.
why: Near-instant runs and one config file. Less time arguing with tooling, more time writing the thing.
audience: JS/TS teams tired of juggling ESLint, Prettier, and their conflicting configs across a monorepo.
